summary: Turns the search page into a client component. It reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and renders them in a list.

findings.title: URL query injected as raw HTML
findings.description: The heading puts the q URL parameter into dangerouslySetInnerHTML without escaping. React therefore renders attacker-supplied markup as HTML. An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. That script can steal data or act as the victim. Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect without dependencies refetches forever
findings.description: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each response calls setResults with a new array, which triggers another render and another fetch. The page sends search requests in an endless loop. This loads the catalog API and wastes the user's bandwidth. Give the effect a dependency array containing query.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.description: The early return for an empty query runs before useState and useEffect. The component therefore calls a different number of hooks depending on q. React throws a hooks-order error when q is added or cleared during client navigation. The page then crashes. Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement
findings.description: The change deletes the search form. Without q, the page now only says to type a search term and gives no input. Users who open /search directly have no way to enter a query. Keep the form with the q input on the page, at least when no query is present.

findings.title: Search failure rejection is never handled
findings.description: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok, but the effect chains no catch. The rejected promise floats unhandled. A failed search shows the user an empty list with no error message. The browser also logs an unhandled rejection. Add a catch that records an error state and renders a failure message.
